title: NG5: Branch-source uniqueness Claim is under-proven for targets on an incident edge (breaks Case A)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** solution.tex, proof of Theorem 1, the *Claim (branch source)*, lines 153-164 (logically prior to Case A / Case B).

**The gap (new; distinct location from NG1 = rm-05346-7).** The Claim asserts: for every branch vertex $\alpha$ and every vertex $q$, the shortest $\alpha$-$q$ path in $G'(x)$ is unique. For $q$ internal on $f=cd$ at offset $s$, the proof writes $d(\alpha,q)=\min(D(\alpha,c)+s,\;D(\alpha,d)+(x_f-s))$ and excludes a tie by invoking "(G)/(I) for edge $f$, offset $s$, branch target $q':=\alpha$." But (G) is **defined only for targets $q$ that do NOT lie on the edge** (Definition, lines 102-109). When $\alpha$ is an **endpoint of $f$** -- i.e. $q$ is internal on an edge incident to $\alpha$ -- $\alpha$ lies ON $f$, so (G) imposes nothing and the cited exclusion is vacuous.

**Explicit failure, consistent with (U) and (G).** Take $\alpha=c$. Then $D(c,c)=0$ and
$$d(c,q)=\min\big(s,\;R_f+(x_f-s)\big),\qquad R_f:=D^x(c,d)\ \text{over $c$-$d$ $H$-paths AVOIDING $f$}.$$
If $f$ is redundant ($R_f<x_f$) -- which (U) permits, requiring only that the minimum-weight $c$-$d$ path be unique -- then the tie $s=R_f+(x_f-s)$, i.e. $2s=R_f+x_f$, produces TWO distinct shortest $c$-$q$ paths: the direct on-edge segment (length $s$) and the wrap $c\to\pi\to d\to q$ (length $R_f+x_f-s$), $\pi$ the unique min-weight $c$-$d$ path. This is a genuine non-geodeticity that (U) AND (G), as literally written, fail to exclude.

**Consequence.** The branch-source Claim underpins the WHOLE sufficiency proof: Case A truncates a same-direction double geodesic to "two shortest $a$-$q$ paths, contradicting the Claim," and Case B also leans on it. So the hole is not confined to the same-edge $p,q$ subcase of NG1 -- it already breaks the Claim and hence Case A. Same root cause as NG1 (the off-edge restriction in (G)) but at an earlier, more elementary step the prior pass did not flag.

**To close (also closes NG1).** Extend the quantifier in (G) to ALL targets $q$, including $q$ on $e$ (endpoints and interior), via a closed-form on-edge clause: for each edge $e=ab$ with $R:=D^x(a,b)$ realised by an $H$-path avoiding $e$, forbid
$$R<x_e \ \wedge\ x_e+R\ \text{even}\ \wedge\ R\le x_e-2$$
(from eq. (8): $R=2(r'-r)-x_e$ with $1\le r<r'\le x_e-1$; the endpoint case relaxes the offset range). With (G) so extended, the Claim's exclusion is valid for endpoint targets, Case A is airtight, and sufficiency needs no appeal to check.py.

comments.body:
**Update for the current (revised) solution.tex — NG5 persists, and the fix is now one line.**

Confirmed: the *Claim (branch source)* (current lines 183–194) still excludes the tie $D(\alpha,c)+s=D(\alpha,d)+(x_f-s)$ for $q$ internal on $f=cd$ by citing "(G) for branch target $\alpha$" — invalid when $\alpha\in\{c,d\}$ (then $\alpha$ lies on $f$ and (G) imposes nothing). This breaks **Case A** (line 206) whenever the global target $q$ sits on an edge incident to $a$.

**The revision makes the fix trivial.** The offending regime is precisely Lemma 4's: $\alpha=c$, $d(c,q)=\min(s,\,R_f+(x_f-s))$, and a tie means $2s=R_f+x_f$, i.e. $f$ **redundant** with $x_f+R_f$ **even**. The newly-added **Lemma 4 (No redundant balanced edge)** then yields an off-edge branch-target (G)-violation — a contradiction with (G). So the Claim is *true* under (U)∧(G); the writeup just needs to add, in the $\alpha\in\{c,d\}$ sub-case, the same Lemma-4 citation already used to patch Case B (NG1, lines 217–236). The author patched Case B but forgot the parallel branch-source Claim.

**Recommended edit.** In the Claim's proof, split on $\alpha\notin\{c,d\}$ (existing (G) citation valid) vs $\alpha\in\{c,d\}$ (cite Lemma 4).
